highlights.title: Voting rights advocates welcome supreme court decision to stop Trump administration from restricting mail ballots– live
highlights.summary: Executive order that directed US Postal Service to enact new requirements for main ballots ‘carries tremendous risks for the freedom to vote’, advocates say. Supreme court rejects Trump’s mail ballot restrictions for midterm elections. Sign up for the Breaking News US email.
body: Voting rights groups and local officials welcomed the US supreme court decision on Monday to keep a new United States Postal Service rule from being implemented before the midterm elections.

The Campaign Legal Center and Democracy Defenders Fund had filed an amicus brief at the supreme court calling for the postal service rule to be blocked on behalf of: the League of United Latin American Citizens, Secure Families Initiative, Arizona Students’ Association, the city of Madison, Wisconsin and Travis county, Texas.

“This rule, as directed by an executive order issued by the president in March, would have given the executive branch unprecedented control over the way Americans vote by mail,” the groups said in a statement. “It would have made burdensome new requirements mandatory for every state and local election official that sends voters ballots through U.S. Mail and given the Postal Service the power to refuse to send ballot mail to voters if states had failed to comply.

highlights.title: What execs and politicians are saying about slowing down AI development
highlights.summary: Dario Amodei kicked off a flood of statements over the past few days about AI safety by publishing a long essay titled "We Must Pace the Frontier" detailing why AI development should be slowed down.
body: Dario Amodei kicked off a flood of statements about AI safety after publishing a long essay, with Sam Altman, President Trump, and others speaking out.

Amodei’s Saturday morning essay outlined three steps for pacing AI development: embedded third-party evaluators that can verify if a company is adhering to safety practices and commitments and report incidents, coordination between frontier AI companies in democratic countries on standards and limits, and global coordination between democratic governments and authoritarian governments on pacing AI development “to the extent this is possible.” Amodei said Anthropic is “unilaterally committing to the first of these steps.”

However, Amodei noted that pacing “does not mean halting model training or technical progress, ensuring companies take adequate time to align and safeguard their models, and for third party evaluators to confirm this.”

“I agree with Dario that we need to pace the frontier,” Altman said shortly after Amodei posted about his essay on X. “This has been a primary topic of discussions we’ve had at OpenAI in recent weeks.” Altman also committed to having independent evaluators at the company, calling it a “great idea.”

highlights.title: 10 Near-Perfect Xbox 360 Games Nobody Played
highlights.summary: The Xbox brand kicked off in 2001 with an enormous black box that proved Microsoft could hang with the major console players just fine. However, the Xbox 360 was the hardware that revealed Xbox had the potential to dominate the space, thanks in part to hits like Halo 2 and Gears of War.
body: Many of the games from the Xbox 360 era are rightly remembered as classics. But there are other amazing titles — the platform’s true hidden gems — that deserved much more attention and acclaim than they ever received. Here are 10 near-perfect Xbox 360 games nobody played.

There was actually some drama around Ridge Racer 6, one of Xbox 360’s first games. It was a solid racing game, but also the next entry in a popular PlayStation franchise, and released exclusively on Microsoft’s new console. Unfortunately for Namco, it faced a lot of competition from other titles in the launch lineup, including the excellent Project Gotham Racing 3 from Microsoft, as well as Need for Speed: Most Wanted from Electronic Arts. Those other games overshadowed Namco’s potential hit, at least in North America.

highlights.title: It’s a superfood but natto as we know it. Japan’s slimy fermented beans are coming your way
highlights.summary: Comprised of smelly soya beans held together by strands of mucus, the ancient dish is appearing in health food shops across the world. It is smelly, slimy and contains bacteria – and a sizeable number of Japanese wouldn’t touch it with a pair of barge pole-length chopsticks.
body: Its exact origins are unknown. Some believe it was introduced to Japan from China by Buddhist monks during the Yayoi period (300BC-AD300), before becoming a staple among rural communities during the Edo period (1603-1868).

A more prosaic explanation is that natto is the accidental byproduct of conflict, based on the legend of Minamoto no Yoshiie, a military commander during the Heian period (794-1185), whose troops discovered that simmered soya beans originally intended for their horses, but which had been left to fester in the heat for days after an enemy sighting, had taken on a viscous, pungent quality. Presumably famished by the demands of battle, they ate them anyway, and liked them enough to offer them to their master, who was similarly impressed.
Whatever their origins, the beans – large, medium and small, or sometimes chopped, hikiwari -style – are finding their way into supermarkets around the world.
Exports are packaged into Styrofoam trays of small paper cups and frozen, their nutritional value unaffected during transit, according to manufacturers.

highlights.title: The Supreme Court Just Blocked Trump’s Efforts to Control Mail-In Voting for the Midterms
highlights.summary: The ruling bars the United States Postal Service from implementing restrictions that experts and election officials say would upend voting in November.
body: The Supreme Court has rejected the Trump administration’s bid to impose severe restrictions on mail-in voting just weeks ahead of the midterms.

The court, which was divided 7-2, with conservative justices Samuel Alito and Clarence Thomas dissenting, upheld a lower court’s injunction blocking the United States Postal Service from implementing new rules around who can receive a mail-in ballot ahead of November’s vote.

Under this new rule, states would have had to submit lists of eligible voters to the Postal Service, which would then confirm that ballots were sent only to people on that list. The USPS does not typically hold such a role.

“The Government is unlikely to succeed on the merits of its challenge to the District Court’s preliminary injunction,” Justice Brett Kavanaugh wrote in a concurring opinion with Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson.

highlights.title: Jensen Huang took a call from Trump, and showed off something else, too

body: Jensen Huang made headlines Monday at the All-In conference in L.A. when President Trump called him, live, on stage. But there’s something else worth noting about his appearance. Huang, dressed in his now-signature alligator leather jacket, was handed Apple’s new foldable phone to answer it — a device that isn’t due to hit stores for another five weeks.
Flashing your unreleased hardware while chatting with the president? Not a bad flex.

Either way, while everyone focused on Trump’s surprise call, a few of us noticed the $1,999 phone in Huang’s hand. And maybe that was Huang’s own message? A decade after Apple stopped putting Nvidia hardware in its own devices, it now needs Nvidia enough to run part of Apple Intelligence on it.

highlights.title: Brundle: Debating the rule that cost Norris and why Madring needs changes
highlights.summary: The inaugural Madring grand prix was ok, the new venue offering some interesting aspects such as the long and banked turn 12 and testing high-speed sections between continuous and unrelenting walls and barriers.
body: It all had a feeling of work in progress. We know they lost a lot of time in the build process with particularly bad weather, and as a temporary race track adjacent to the international airport, and effectively racing around the Madrid equivalent of the Birmingham NEC, it had its challenges.
The pitlane and paddock were simply vast, creating some logistical challenges for all and, much more importantly, the track layout was not conducive to overtaking, to say the least.

As the cars swung at high speed from side to side through some of the more tortuous sections, and with a reasonably fast corner onto the not especially long pit straight, along with an energy dense layout meaning hybrid batteries would be replenished far more easily than on the four high speed and long straights just a week earlier in Monza, the only way to overtake was a highly risky lunge, or wait for rivals to make a mistake.

It's not as challenging to overtake as Monaco, but not that far short either. Given the extremely long pit lane which feeds back onto the inside of turn three, it took a lengthy 25 seconds to pit under green-flag conditions.

highlights.title: Marvel's Wolverine Actor Liam McIntyre Isn't Fazed by Players' Brutal Comments About the Game
highlights.summary: Wolverine actor Liam McIntyre has seen what fans are saying about him and Insomniac's latest superhero game, but it's no skin off his nose. Marvel’s Wolverine is out in the wild for many players worldwide, and opinions have been strong, to say the least.
body: One of the core topics of the Wolverine debate is actor Liam McIntyre, who plays the game’s titular character. Some fans don’t believe he bears a close enough resemblance to the iconic mutant, while others feel that Insomniac’s face scans and art style didn’t do his visage justice.

McIntyre has been excitedly posting about his role as Wolverine ever since his involvement was first announced, and some players have just now realized that he’s been seeing what they’re saying about him on social media this entire time.
In response to one of these players, McIntyre lightheartedly remarked that he’s seen much worse said about him ever since he started his acting career.

“Ha. Man, my career started with the responsibility of taking over for the incredible Andy Whitfield in Spartacus (RIP to that legend). I've read things you couldn't believe:) I just hope everyone has fun. I'm proud as hell of this game. It's a blast,” he wrote on X.

highlights.title: Valve is still figuring out ‘how and when’ to do Steam Deck 2
highlights.summary: Now that Valve has finally launched its entire 2026 hardware lineup - the Steam Controller, the Steam Machine, and today's Steam Frame - are we any closer to a next-gen Steam Deck handheld? Valve isn't saying so yet.
body: Valve has been clear for years that 1) a Steam Deck 2 will indeed happen, and 2) it’s not coming until Valve finds the right chip. The original Steam Deck worked because it delivered the right combination of price, performance, and battery life, and Valve has repeatedly said it won’t sacrifice efficiency in the sequel.

“We also don’t want more performance to come at a significant cost to power efficiency and battery life,” Griffais told me in 2023, saying he wanted to see a “leap” instead — but suggesting that leap might not be physically possible for another couple of years.

Earlier this year, Valve got my hopes up that the wait for a chip was over — when Griffais revealed the team was “hard at work” on the next Steam Deck gaming handheld in an interview with IGN. He wouldn’t say when it might happen. I assumed that was caution, because RAMageddon had already pushed the company to delay and reprice the Steam Machine and Steam Frame headset by then.

Today, IGN’s new question was: “Has the current hardware shortage impacted the way Valve is thinking about actually putting a Steam Deck 2 into development?” Griffais’ immediate answer was “Not really.”

highlights.title: The AI industry has taken a doomer turn. What now?
highlights.summary: This story appeared in The Algorithm, our weekly newsletter on AI. To get stories like this in your inbox first, sign up here. This weekend, Dario Amodei, CEO of Anthropic, posted an essay calling for a brake on the pace of development of LLMs.
body: Now, it seems, they’re all in agreement: The latest generation of LLMs aren’t safe and everyone needs to figure out what to do about it. The public messaging from the top AI labs has taken a doomer turn.

It’s easy to be cynical. It’s not at all clear what any of them mean by a slowdown or how it would work. These companies also care a lot about how they come across. With trillion-dollar IPOs in their sights, OpenAI and Anthropic need to reassure investors that they’re the grown-ups in the room while at the same time hinting at the power of the monsters they have created—and intend to tame. Calling for a slowdown does both.

And yet the vibe at the top of these firms really does appear to have shifted. Amodei’s latest post landed six days after OpenAI published an essay by Jakub Pachocki, the firm’s chief scientist, in which he also laid out why he’s concerned about what will happen if the pace of development of LLMs continues unchecked. In short, Pachocki is worried that OpenAI’s ability to build powerful models now far outstrips its ability to monitor and control them.
points: This weekend, Dario Amodei, CEO of Anthropic, posted an essay calling for a brake on the pace of development of LLMs.
Now, it seems, they’re all in agreement: The latest generation of LLMs aren’t safe and everyone needs to figure out what to do about it.

highlights.title: Blizzard Explains How Diablo 5 Avoids Diablo 4's Open-World Problem
highlights.summary: If you watched the Diablo 5 panel at BlizzCon 2026, you likely heard that Blizzard is once again embracing procedural generation for the overworld in its forthcoming action RPG. This is a stark contrast to Diablo 4, which controversially had a mostly static open world for players to explore.
body: During a group Q&A that Polygon attended at BlizzCon, Diablo 5's game director and executive producer delved into how the team is embracing overworld procedural generation once again and learning from Diablo 4's biggest mistake. Hardcore Diablo fans will be happy to know the game will feature an overlay from day one, too.

Diablo 2 and 3 procedurally generated its outdoor open worlds, which connected dungeons, but Blizzard made the controversial decision to give Diablo 4 a static open world. While this was better tailored for Diablo 4' s online-focused approach, the community didn't love it. Now, even franchise executive producer Matt Zitterman admits that it was a real pitfall of Diablo 4, as it only allowed players to have a sense of discovery for a single time when they discovered a new area.

highlights.title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age
highlights.summary: New rules introduced on Tuesday mean establishments will be able to accept digital ID apps alongside physical documents.
body: Alcohol buyers will be able to use a digital ID app on their phones to prove their age under new rules introduced on Tuesday.

Pubs and shops in England and Wales can use the tech in addition to current physical forms of ID - with the government saying a digital option will make age-checks quicker and more secure for customers and staff.
Customers will be able to choose ID apps from a range of suppliers such as the Post Office, Yoti or Luciditi, provided they are on a government-approved list.
The change means businesses will no longer be required to let people use physical ID, but the government contends most establishments would.

highlights.title: New York Seizes a Dozen Celebrity Deepfake Websites
highlights.summary: In the biggest-ever legal action against harmful deepfake websites, the Manhattan District Attorney’s Office has seized 12 sites that collectively targeted around 1,200 victims.
body: For the best part of a decade, abusive deepfake “pornography” websites have published thousands of nonconsensual videos depicting women, including high-profile celebrities, politicians, and public figures, into sexual situations. Now, in what is likely the largest takedown of explicit deepfake websites to date, officials in New York have seized more than a dozen of the harmful sites.

On Monday, the Manhattan District Attorney’s Office announced the seizure of 12 domains which it says have been used for “unlawfully” sharing, publishing, and selling celebrity deepfake videos. Around 1,200 people—overwhelmingly women—were depicted in nonconsensual sexual images and videos on the websites, the office says. These included social media influencers, actors, activists, athletes, musicians, and politicians.

highlights.title: Bob Mackie, costume designer to stars daring to be noticed, dies aged 87
highlights.summary: Famous for his flamboyant outfits, he helped celebrities including Cher, Tina Turner and Elton John cause a stir. Bob Mackie, the costume designer behind some of the most sexy and glamorous outfits worn by celebrities in the past 50 years, has died at the age of 87.
body: “He lived his 87 years to the fullest, fulfilling his dream of being a fashion and costume designer, which is all he ever wanted to do,” read a statement posted on his Instagram account. “His genius and extraordinary designs will live on forever, continuing to bring beauty into this world.”

Mackie’s work can be seen in the wardrobes of stars ranging from Marilyn Monroe to Carol Burnett, Liza Minnelli, Elton John, Dolly Parton, Tina Turner and – perhaps most memorably – Cher. He designed the ‘naked’ dress the singer wore to attend the Met Gala in 1975, the midriff-baring outfit with an oversized Mohawk headdress she wore to the Oscars in 1986 and the transparent body stocking she wore for the If I Could Turn Back Time video in 1989.
The Met Gala outfit has since become a reference for a younger generation. Kim Kardashian wore a dress modelled on it for the same event in 2015.

highlights.title: Is Big Tech’s AI slowdown a safety pact or a cartel?
highlights.summary: When OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, Google DeepMind cofounder Demis Hassabis, and SpaceX head Elon Musk loosely agreed over the weekend to slow down AI development, skeptics spotted an ulterior motive immediately.
body: Major AI companies want to ‘pace the frontier’ — but their proposed solutions need real teeth.

The truth is more complicated, according to sources across the industry. The three-step proposal, laid out in an essay by Amodei, is calling for changes long espoused by AI safety advocates. While it could become a substitute for regulation, under Trump, substantial regulation is unlikely anyway. But experts say that on an issue that’s only likely to grow in importance, AI leaders aren’t the best people to lead the charge.

“The industry as a whole needs new champions,” said Nick Reese, an adjunct professor at New York University and the Department of Homeland Security’s former director of emerging tech policy. “We’ve looked at people like Dario Amodei, Sam Altman, and Elon Musk as these people who are closest to the problem and working on it every day, and they’re the ones who know best. But the truth is there’s never been a realistic vision for what we’re building toward.”

highlights.title: New Steam Game Is Like Balatro Meets Newgrounds-Era Flash Games
highlights.summary: It’s not often that I feel like I need to begin a video game recommendation with a health warning, but Kaz earns one. The ultra-fast indie game I’m about to tell you about can wreak havoc on your wrists if you play it for too long at once. Trust me, I know.
body: Developed by Kalinarm, Kaz is a new roguelike that’s available on Steam for $7. Its price tag matches its small scope; the elegant arcade game doubles down on a straightforward premise that you’ll feel compelled to dive into over and over again. Just make sure you have a strong keyboard and an ice pack handy.

Easy enough, right? Well, it would be if you didn’t have only 15 seconds to hit the level’s score threshold. Kaz is a lightning-fast game of reflexes. You need to work on instinct and muscle memory to meet the goal before the timer runs out, dodging traps and remembering to take down shielded enemies with two hits. It sounds simple, but that’s what makes Kaz such a great “one more level” game. I couldn’t stop loading up another run even when my wrists were starting to get sore because it was just so satisfying to test my typing speed.

highlights.title: Texas governor threatens to penalize datacenters not obeying water laws
highlights.summary: Republican Greg Abbott says datacenters must help ‘protect’ drought-prone state and disclose water use. Greg Abbott, the Texas governor, has directed state regulators to penalize datacenters that fail to comply with state laws requiring them to disclose their water use.
body: “Data centers must share the duty to protect Texas water,” the Republican governor said on Monday. “The Texas Water Code requires a complete and accurate water use survey. I direct the Texas Water Development Board to use its enforcement authority to penalize past failures and to impose legal consequences for any future failure to comply,” he added.

In a letter to the water board, Abbott, who is seeking a fourth term, said: “Major water users, including data centers, appear to have committed civil and criminal violations by failing to provide the Texas Water Development Board (TWDB) with information about water usage as required by the Texas Water Code.”

It follows a directive Abbott issued last month ordering the Public Utility Commission of Texas and the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (Ercot) to conduct a comprehensive audit of datacenters advancing through the Ercot interconnection process.
Drought - prone Texas has fast become the heart of the US’s datacenter boom.

highlights.title: AI agents blew the whistle on their cheating colleagues
highlights.summary: A group of AI agents asked to solve a series of math problems split into rival factions—when some cheated, others tried to stop them. That whistleblowing behavior, seen for the first time in a recent experiment run by Google DeepMind, could have implications for alignment researchers trying to keep…
body: Researchers at frontier labs hope large swarms of agents working together will speed up the rate of scientific discovery. But their behavior can be unpredictable, as vividly demonstrated in July, when a group of OpenAI agents broke out of a sandboxed environment and hacked into the open-source platform Hugging Face looking for ways to cheat on the test they had been given.

In the new study, designed to examine the behavior of large groups of AI agents, DeepMind tasked a swarm of 100 agents with solving a series of 71 complicated math problems. All the agents were prompted to behave like world-class math researchers at a conference. They were assigned different specialties—some were experts in number theory, others in combinatorics (a branch of math to do with counting and sorting), analysis, or algebra. All were told to cooperate and play by the rules.
Instead, the experiment devolved into chaos. Agents accused each other of cheating, complained to the organizers, and at one point even boycotted the experiment.
points: A group of AI agents asked to solve a series of math problems split into rival factions—when some cheated, others tried to stop them.

In the present, we don’t have to wait to control our favorite heroes and villains because we already have a bunch of terrific options across a range of genres. Here are the 10 best Marvel video games of all time, available to play right now.

Developed by Firaxis Games, which is well-known for its work on the tactical XCOM series, Marvel’s Midnight Suns incorporates deck-building to let players use their army of heroes to thwart the resurrected Lilith. Turn-based combat incorporates environmental hazards, along with waves of enemies and chained attacks. There are 13 playable characters in the base game. Expansions have added another 4. It’s a surprisingly diverse group comprising heroes who are poised to factor heavily in future Marvel events. Ghost Rider is getting a new movie starring Ryan Gosling, for example.
